title: Resource Compatibility in Optimal Quantum Symmetry Testing
authors: Yimeng Cao, Ranyiliu Chen, Chengkai Zhu, Xin Wang
abstract: Can a symmetry be tested optimally without using the quantum resource naturally associated with it? For parallel subgroup-versus-Haar testing, we derive a quantitative representation-theoretic converse for every protocol with zero type-I error: the excess type-II error is bounded below by the sum of two nonnegative penalties, one for weight on suboptimal subgroup types and one for deviations of within-type Schur profiles from their typewise extremal profiles. At optimality, both penalties vanish, yielding support and weight locking for every optimal system marginal. Disjointness of the resulting locked set and the free marginal set rules out resource-free optimality, whereas overlap alone does not establish attainability. For the diagonal torus in dimension $d\geq 2$, optimal testing without coherence is possible only with a single query. We determine both the exact optimal type-II error over all protocols with incoherent system marginals and the minimum system-marginal coherence required to attain the unrestricted optimum. For the orthogonal subgroup in dimension $d\geq 2$, a real protocol attains the optimum at every query number. For the qutrit Clifford group, Wigner-positive optimal protocols exist at three and four queries but not from five through nine; whether they exist beyond nine queries remains open. Together, these results relate the subgroup- and query-dependent resource requirements of optimal symmetry testing to structural constraints on optimal system marginals.
summary: This work develops a rigorous framework to quantify the resource cost in optimal quantum symmetry testing. By deriving representation-theoretic bounds, the authors prove that achieving the best possible error rate often requires the system marginal to possess specific structural properties, such as high coherence or support restricted to certain sectors. This deepens the understanding of resource compatibility in quantum information tasks.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether optimal quantum symmetry testing can be achieved without utilizing the quantum resource inherently associated with the symmetry group.
main_result: The authors derive quantitative bounds showing that resource-free optimality is generally impossible, and they establish specific minimum coherence requirements for achieving the optimum in certain cases.
method: The analysis uses representation theory, deriving a converse bound on the excess type-II error based on penalties related to suboptimal types and deviations in Schur profiles.
model_or_system: The model involves testing a unitary $U$ belonging to a specific subgroup $G$ (like the diagonal torus or orthogonal subgroup) against the Haar measure on $U(d)$, using $m$-query parallel protocols.
key_observables: Type-I and Type-II error probabilities ($\alpha,  eta$), system marginal ($ho$), and representation-theoretic scores ($h_m(\eta)$).
important_parameters: The number of queries ($m$), the dimension ($d$), and the coherence measure ($C_{	ext{rel}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes zero type-I error ($\alpha=0$) to derive the lower bounds on the type-II error.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables detailing spectral phase-order bounds, exact scaled coefficients for different groups, and the structure of active Schur sectors for various query numbers.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general representation-theoretic converse bound, applying this to specific groups (torus, orthogonal, Clifford), and finally analyzing the resource requirements (coherence, number of queries) needed to approach the theoretical optimum.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous mathematical tools (representation theory, error bounding) to quantify the fundamental resource costs associated with distinguishing quantum states based on underlying symmetries, which is crucial for quantum characterization tasks.
